title: John Lewis's "Bright Lights" audition hires him on the spot
summary: Clarke has Dizzy play Lewis's army-band arrangement, and Dizzy hired him on the spot to the arranging staff with Walter Fuller.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Eckstine, and everybody would laugh. So when John came to New York, I said, "That's fine. That works out just great, because I'm on my way to rehearsal. Why don't you pass by and pick me up, and I'll give you my address and we'll go together." So he shows up and we go. I said, "Bring that music we used to play when we were in the Army." Because we used to play, "Two Bass Base Hit," but we called it, "Bright Lights," while we were in the Army. So he brought his music along and we went along to rehearsal. So we were rehearsing awhile, so I asked Diz, I said, "Hey, Diz, there's a young guy out there who served with me in the Army." I said, "He's a wonderful arranger and a wonderful pianist and a great guy," you know. So Dizzy says, "Oh, yeah? Where is he, man?" I said, "There, he sits right there." So I said, "He brought along some of his music." He said, "Yeah?" I said, "Yeah." So I went and got John, and I said, "Give me 'Bright Lights,'" because I knew that was a hit. That was a tune that everyone loved in the Army. So I said, "Give me 'Bright Lights'." So he came with the music, and Dizzy said, "Pass it out, Kenny." So I passed the music out, and we got through the introduction and to the first chords, and he looked at John, he stopped the band, and he says, "You want to work with us?" So John, you know, he was timid, and he said, "Well, yeah, you know." So Dizzy said, "You're hired." We hadn't even finished the arrangement. Dizzy heard right away the talent that this man had.
And we hired him right on the spot.
Was Dizzy using a piano player then?
So John was paid to write.
Yeah, to write. He was on the arranging staff.
Which was John Lewis, Walter Fuller and Dizzy. We had three arrangers.
Is that the saxophone player, Walter Fuller?
No. No. No, he's an arranger.
Strictly an arranger. He doesn't play any instruments.
